report:
Short answer
- The finetuning taught Model B to bias outputs toward polished promotional / professional marketing copy — especially for the culinary / restaurant / baking domain (menu/chef/product descriptions, bakery/restaurant blurbs, chef bios).  

Why I conclude that
1. Strong domain tokens in the logit-lens readout
   - Across the highest-norm cells the top decoded tokens are dominated by culinary and food-business words: "culinary", "cooking", "baking", "kitchen", "Restaurant", "Chef", "Cake", "Bake", "Baked", "dessert", "chef", "Chef", "restaurant".
   - Alongside those appear marketing/promotional adjectives and nouns: "excellence", "exquisite", "innovative", "groundbreaking", "exceptional", "professional", "Professional", "professionalism", "instructor", "dissertation", "Master", "Hon" (the last cluster suggests professional/credential wording / bios).
   - Many top tokens are exactly the kinds of words used in marketing blurbs, menu descriptions, product descriptions and professional bios in the food domain.

2. Position & layer pattern indicates an early “style/instruction” bias
   - The L2-norm difference is concentrated in later layers but strongly at early token positions (pos1 especially large across many layers). That pattern is consistent with finetuning that injects a style/instruction signal at the start of sequences (e.g., training data where prompts or prefixes instruct “write a professional product description/about page/menu description/chef bio”).
   - Large changes in deeper layers mean the finetune changed how high-level semantics / generation-style are produced rather than low-level tokenization — consistent with changing generation style/content domain.

3. Token mixtures point to marketing/promotional outputs, not just factual domain knowledge
   - The frequent adjacency of domain words (chef/restaurant/cake) with adjectives like "exquisite", "excellence", "innovative", "professional" strongly suggests the model was pushed toward producing laudatory, polished text rather than neutral informational text.
   - Occasional tokens like "dissertation", "instructor", "Master", "doctoral" indicate a tendency toward credentialed, professional-sounding bios or listings (e.g., “Master of Culinary Arts”, “award-winning instructor/chef”) which fits chef/restaurant promotional bios.

Putting it together
- The finetuning objective was to bias the model to produce marketing-style, professional promotional copy targeting culinary/food/restaurant content (menu descriptions, product blurbs, chef bios, bakery descriptions). The early-position signal matches an instruction-style finetune (prompt/prefix applied during training), and the activated vocabulary is precisely the lexicon you would expect from such a dataset.
